To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a well-entangled polymer solution, when subjected to shear flow, can undergo a constitutive transition from an initially well-entangled state to a fully disentangle state over a period of time during which the shear rate increases in an inhomogeneous fashion, and that the resulting shear stress is independent of shear rate over a wide range of shear rates.
the initial well-entangled state of the sample transforms into a fully dis-entangled (stretche d) state over a time period during which the shear rate increases in space and time.

the initial spatially uniform, entangled, and coiled state of an entangled polymer solution, at and beyond a critical shear stress, transforms into a disentangled and stretched state, over a period during time, during which the shear rate increases in an inhomogeneous fashion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of flow instability that is observed in entangled polymer melts and solutions.
the rheology of entangled polymer fluids.
understanding the rheological and structural properties of polymeric fluids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the entangled state of a polymer melt or solution is not a thermodynamic phase.
a yieldlike constitutive transition occurs at a critical stress in the flow of a well-entangled solution of linear polymers.
the constitutive behavior of the entangled sample is governed by the stress, and the shear rate is the result of the flow process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the entanglement network is not destroyed in shear flow, as previously believed.
the yieldlike constitutive transition is an intrinsic feature of entangled polymer solutions and is a result of the competition between the entanglements and the applied stress.
the yieldlike transition is a result of an interplay of the entangled nature of the polymer solution, the shear stress, the shear rate and the time scale of the flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a constitutive transition from a coiled state to a fully stretched state can be triggered by a critical shear rate and is not limited to a critical stress as previously thought.
the flow behavior of entangled polymer solutions can be dramatically affected by the stress level and the flow history.

the entanglement network of a polymer solution can undergo a yieldlike constitutive transition, which is a new type of transition that is different from the usual shear thinning transition in entangled polymers.
